Keywords: Tales and witnesses at woodland waters
RagShortTexts: People tell water and woodland stories about danger.
A teller distinguishes personal experience from hearsay.

Variants.Content: Villagers tell strange stories of water and woods: some fear taboos, others use tales to warn children. Versions differ. Deep water, unfamiliar forest and night travel pose tangible risks, prompting questions about place and witnesses.
Night guards check sounds together rather than pursue alone. Belief differs within a unit; ridiculing frightened companions can damage discipline more than a tale.
Taboos affect willingness to guide or work. Understanding a particular concern and alternatives preserves cooperation better than dismissing an entire village.
Stories warn children away from dangerous water, though neighbors differ. A missing person still needs boats, ropes and searchers familiar with the place.
